text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Auto-detected anomaly: sustained GPU allocation failures in prod-us-west1. Metric triggers: `gpu_alloc_fail_rate > 15%` for 5m and `scheduler_queue_length > 600`. Paging oncall.

Lina O.: I'm on it. First pass: queue exploded from ~90 -> 760 in ~7m. Cluster shows ~88% aggregate GPU-util but 27% of GPU capacity is 'stranded' (not addressable due to MIG fragmentation).

Raj SRE: pulling scheduler traces. Repeated failures look like: `allocation_rejected: contiguous_slice_unavailable` for 1.5g requests. Recent maintenance (yesterday) applied mixed MIG profiles to save cost (0.5g + 1g per node). That change increased slice heterogeneity; the binpacker can't place 1.5g units efficiently.

Priya Eng: confirmed client-side symptoms: model=v2.0-chat-large saw elevated 429s and enqueue latencies. Telemetry: effective throttles jumped to 9.4% at peak. Notably, autoscaler kept requesting new instances but cloud API returned `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: quota_burst` intermittently.

Marco PM: customer visibility? CS-ops, any inbound?

CS-ops: customers reporting timeouts. Two high-tier customers submitted support tickets; one flagged as possible SLA violation. We drafted an acknowledgement. No data loss reported.

Lina O.: Triage plan (short): 1) remove new allocations from fragmented pool-gpu-mix, 2) reroute heavy customers to reserved-dedicated-capacity temporarily, 3) apply conservative placement-relax so smaller slices can be combined for larger requests, 4) request cloud burst quota increase. Executing now.

Raj SRE: cordoning nodes in pool-gpu-mix and triggering controlled eviction of spot/low-priority jobs to free cleaner nodes. Command:```bash
kubectl label nodes pool-gpu-mix-* redwood/temp-no-alloc=true --overwrite
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l tier=low -o name); do kubectl delete $pod --grace-period=5; done
```
Progress: evicted 62 low-priority pods, freed ~35 GPU-minutes.

Infra-bot: Cloud quota check: current burst quota used 100%; request submitted to provider ticket #CB-5542. Estimated human review 60-120m.

Priya Eng: hot patch deployed to scheduler: `allow_slice_merging=true` to permit splitting/merging of smaller MIG slices for allocation simulation. This is risky: can increase per-request latency and increases KV cache fragmentation. Patch applied to canary nodes at 03:47 UTC.

Raj SRE: after patch, allocation rejects dropped ~70% in canary. Logs:```
[2026-03-14T03:49:12Z] alloc_attempt id=xyz result=split_merge_alloc node=pool-gpu-mix-7
[2026-03-14T03:50:01Z] alloc_attempt id=abc result=success node=pool-gpu-mix-3
```

Lina O.: routing change: shifting top-15 customers to dedicated-reserved-us-west1; weights lowered for general traffic to reduce pressure. Implemented via routing-control at 03:55 UTC.

CS-ops: customer update sent at 04:05 UTC: apology + short mitigation steps + ETA for broader recovery 2-4h. Two customers asked for immediate credit; case opened.

Marco PM: need clear next steps for full recovery and root cause avoid. Lina, Raj, can you estimate time to reprovision pool as homogeneous?

Raj SRE: reprovision plan created: reprovision 14 nodes in pool-gpu-mix to uniform 1.5g MIG layout, replaced in batches of 4. Cloud provisioning ETA ~70-100m per batch due to global provisioning backlog. Total ETA ~3.5h. Will proceed after confirming routing and canary stability.

Priya Eng: additional mitigation: temporarily scale up reserved-dedicated nodes by 8 to absorb immediate high-priority requests. Doing this now via infra API; expected ready in ~8m.

incident-bot: @Raj SRE assigned as incident lead for infra actions.

Raj SRE: note - autoscaler behavior: when allocation fails frequently, autoscaler currently assumes insufficient total capacity and requests more instances. With fragmentation, requests fail despite spare overall GPU compute. Need a short-term tweak: recognize fragmentation signature and prefer reshuffle/eviction before new instance requests. Applying autoscaler fork with `prefer_reshuffle_on_fragmentation=true` to canary autoscalers at 04:15 UTC.

Priya Eng: after autoscaler tweak and placement patch, queue length started decreasing slowly: 760 -> 310 in ~25m. Throttles down to ~1.8%. Observed slight increase in per-request tail latency (+8-12%) on affected models.

Lina O.: handoff to follow-up rotation at 05:30 UTC. Handoff note: cluster stable enough for on-call to stand down, reprovision ongoing. If queue increases >400 or throttles >3% reopen P1.

CS-ops: second customer communication sent at 05:40 UTC with more details and offer for credits for impacted requests.

Marco PM: action items captured: 1) revert mixed-MIG experiment and lock pool-gpu-mix to homogeneous layouts, 2) add admission-test in CI that simulates mixed-slice binpacking, 3) change autoscaler heuristics to detect fragmentation pattern, 4) author clear ops runbook for 'fragmentation spike' including placement-relax and reserved-capacity spillover. Owners assigned.

Raj SRE: final status 06:12 UTC - reprovision batch 1 completed, cluster healthy metrics trending to baseline; queue at 95, throttle ~0.2%. Leaving `allow_slice_merging` enabled for 2h as safety net, then revert. Cloud quota still under review but not blocking since we used reserved capacity.

Lina O.: closing note 07:12 UTC - incident mitigated. Root cause: recent mixed MIG layout increased fragmentation, autoscaler misinterpreted failures as lack of overall capacity and attempted scale-up under cloud burst quota limits, causing delays and sustained queue growth. Mitigations: routing to reserved capacity, eviction of low-priority workloads, scheduler placement relax, autoscaler heuristic patch, and targeted reprovision to homogeneous MIG layout. Postmortem owner: Raj SRE. Timeline doc: https://internal.redwood/incident/1772004320.

CS-ops: summary for postmortem: 5 key customers affected, peak throttles ~9.4%, no data loss, credits requested by two customers.

incident-bot: Incident 1772004320 status -> mitigated. Reply `reopen 1772004320` to reopen. :white_check_mark:
